title: Catalog manifest harmonization + stamped performance signatures for new model arrivals
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: New model ingestions vary in metadata fields, version identifiers, and performance artifacts. PMs and SDKs must be able to reliably resolve a model id -> pinned version + performance signature (latency/cost/quality) so customers can pin and we can fall back safely.

Goal: Produce an engineering deliverable that: (1) introduces a small compatibility layer (catalog manifest v2.1) for newly onboarded models, (2) enforces a stamped performance-signature object in the catalog publish flow, and (3) updates onboarding docs and the public model metadata page. The solution must avoid breaking existing pinned deployments and include a migration plan for manifests added in the prior 6 months.
acceptance_criteria: A catalog manifest v2.1 is defined with backward-compatible fields and documented in the onboarding playbook.
Onboarding pipeline requires a performance_signature file (sha + metadata) before publishing a model to staging.
Console and model-catalog APIs surface the stamped performance signature and pin suggestions for each variant.
Automated tests validate that requests routed to pinned variants use the variant fingerprint and fall back to compatible variants on mismatch.
Onboarded models for the last 6 months are retrofitted with best-effort performance signatures and a migration flag is present in the manifest.
implementation_steps: Design manifest v2.1 schema and compatibility rules (schema doc in Confluence).
Add performance_signature generation step to ingestion pipeline (bench + sniff).
Modify catalog publish service to reject publish if signature missing for new model submissions; allow optional for legacy via migration flag.
Expose signature and pin-recommendation in /catalog/model/:id endpoint and Console model detail page.
Add end-to-end tests: ingestion -> publish -> pin -> runtime routing with simulated latency curves.
Run migration job for models ingested in last 6 months to attach approximate signatures and set manifest.migration="true".
Update onboarding doc and quickstart with examples and troubleshooting.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Generating an authoritative performance signature requires running short benchmarks on representative hardware which increases onboarding time by ~10-15 minutes. We will make benchmarking parallelizable and optional for non-critical models to preserve velocity.

Compatibility decision: Keep manifest v2.1 additive. Existing runtime will read fallback fields and accept older manifests. This avoids a forced migration but requires runtime checks for presence/absence of signature fields.
Quality: signatures are probabilistic (sampled latency curves). We'll include a confidence score and link to the original bench job for audits.
Cost: Bench jobs consume GPU minutes; limit to smallest recommended batch size and sample set to bound cost. Billing-owner: infra cost center.
rollback_plan: If publish enforcement causes a backlog, revert enforcement flag and run a scheduled migration that attaches signatures asynchronously.
If runtime falls back more frequently than expected, add a temporary routing override to prefer latest stable variant until signatures are re-computed.
Document reversal steps and alert SRE on anomalies.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest v2.1 schema validation with positive/negative cases.
Integration test: ingest a toy model, generate signature, publish, pin, and validate runtime routing with mocked latency distribution.
Load test to ensure publish pipeline can handle 50 concurrent ingestions without resource exhaustion.
End-to-end QA checklist and signoff by PM and Design.
